_comment: Optional: the agent worker's bootstrap, as a file instead of environment.
The agent is a Stalwart account of its own (ADR 0003) — a persona that
works across the groups the operator grants it. GILBERT_AGENT_ADDRESS and
GILBERT_AGENT_PASSWORD in the environment say the same thing; this file is
for a deployment that mounts secrets rather than passing them in, and for
one that keeps the agent's credential out of a process listing.
Point at it with GILBERT_AGENTS_FILE=/etc/gilbert/agents.json. A running
server and a running worker both re-read it as it changes, so editing it
needs no restart. The Gilbert admin surface writes a minted or rotated
secret into it, under the agent's own address, which is what lets naming an
address — and rotating its secret — finish without you carrying anything:
mount it read-write for that, or read-only to keep the surface out and
place the secret here yourself. When both are set the environment wins for
the password.
The password is the agent's own app password. It reaches exactly the
accounts the operator granted the agent in Stalwart's own administration —
membership is the grant, and there is no second, in-product switch. The
Gilbert admin surface verifies the grant per group and says so when it is
missing; it never writes one.
Areas default to all of them. A worker serves only the areas it declares,
which is how a busy installation spreads the work across processes: the
claim unit is account × area, so two workers never touch the same area of
one account. One agent, several workers — not several identities.
Docs: docs/adr/0003-agent-worker-fleet.md
